Jabez
JAY-bez
proper noun
From the Hebrew, connected with the word for sorrow or pain, “he causes pain,” because his mother bore him in sorrow.

Biblical Definition

Jabez appears in a single brief passage tucked within the genealogies of Judah in First Chronicles, yet his record shines for its honour and its prayer. Scripture says he was more honourable than his brethren, though his mother had named him Jabez, saying she bore him in sorrow. Despite a name that marked him with pain from birth, Jabez did not resign himself to sorrow but called on the God of Israel, praying that God would bless him indeed, enlarge his coast, keep His hand upon him, and keep him from evil that it might not grieve him. The text simply adds that God granted him that which he requested. His prayer is no charm or formula for prosperity, as some have wrongly made it, but a humble appeal to the sovereign God who hears His people, asking for blessing, for usefulness, for the LORD’s presence, and above all for keeping from evil. It is the cry of faith that depends wholly on God for everything good and dreads sin more than hardship. That such a man should be honoured above his brethren and singled out in the dry rolls of genealogy testifies that the LORD marks the prayers of the lowly. Jabez teaches that no name and no painful beginning can shut a man out from the grace of a God who answers those who call upon Him in faith.

Webster 1828 Definition

A man of Judah, more honourable than his brethren, whose humble prayer for blessing, enlargement, and keeping from evil God granted.

expand to see more

JABEZ, a man of the tribe of Judah named in the Chronicles genealogy.

Called more honourable than his brethren (1Ch 4:9).

Named by his mother for the sorrow in which she bore him.

Prayed that God would bless him, enlarge his coast, and keep him from evil (1Ch 4:10).

God granted him that which he requested.

Key Scripture

1Ch 4:9 — "And Jabez was more honourable than his brethren: and his mother called his name Jabez, saying, Because I bare him with sorrow."

1Ch 4:10 — "And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me! And God granted him that which he requested."

Psa 34:15 — "The eyes of the LORD are upon the righteous, and his ears are open unto their cry."

Jer 33:3 — "Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not."

Modern Corruption

His prayer, abused by some as a prosperity formula, is in truth the humble appeal of faith to a God who answers those who call.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The error to name here is the misuse of his prayer as a self-help charm for wealth and success. The text shows no formula but a believer casting himself wholly on the God of Israel, asking for blessing, for the LORD’s hand upon him, and above all to be kept from evil lest it grieve him.

Read rightly, Jabez teaches that God hears the cry of the lowly and that no painful beginning can bar a man from grace. His chief petition was holiness, not gain; he dreaded sin more than hardship. The honour Scripture gives him belongs to the faith that prays and the God who answers, not to any technique for prosperity.

Hebrew Roots

A Hebrew name bound to the word for sorrow or pain, given because of a sorrowful birth.

expand to see more

Jabez — Hebrew, linked with sorrow or pain, “he causes pain.”

His mother gave the name because she bore him with sorrow (1Ch 4:9).

A man of the tribe of Judah in the Chronicles genealogy.

A town of scribes in Judah also bore the name Jabez (1Ch 2:55).

His whole record stands in two short verses, yet is among the most quoted of prayers.

Usage

"Jabez was more honourable than his brethren though his name spoke of sorrow."

"The prayer of Jabez asked for blessing and for keeping from evil, not for mere gain."

"Like Jabez, the believer calls on the God of Israel and is heard."
